_comment: Daedalus's policy for its OWN repository. Authorised by Kaya on 2026-07-29. See docs/PROPOSED_SELF_POLICY.md for the reasoning and docs/adrs/ for the write-confinement finding. To revoke: delete this file. There is no other state.
name: agent_env

policy._comment_write_allow: THIS is the write permission. `allow` below is the EGRESS axis and does NOT gate writes -- measured: with allow-only, 8 of 12 paths this policy claims to deny were writable, including daedalus/config.py, which loads this file. write_allow is prefix-anchored at the repo root: an entry ending in / names a subtree, anything else names one file.
policy._comment_egress: Which paths' BYTES may reach an untrusted external API. Separate question from writing, deliberately kept separate.
policy._comment_high_risk: Belt to write_allow's braces, and it does real work even though write_allow already denies these: it forces change_risk -> 'high', which routes the task AWAY from the free local lane before any write is attempted. If somebody widens write_allow later -- and somebody will -- these must still be refused, so that widening has to delete a line that names what it is protecting.

_comment_write_wave_policy: Authorised by Kaya on 2026-07-29: 'standard ist aber automatisch' -- the auto-promote knob for concurrent write waves (daedalus.kairos.gated_writes.run_write_wave), set to 'always' here deliberately, same as the shipped template default. This does NOT bypass the discrimination gate: it is ANDed against daedalus.core.get_governance()'s promotion_allowed every time, which stays FALSE until runs/spine/gate_discrimination.json is fresh against HEAD and proves this repo's test command actually catches a bad patch. Until that receipt exists (or goes stale, as it is right now -- it names an old commit, HEAD has moved), 'always' is armed but inert: every write-wave candidate is held for a human, exactly as 'never' would hold it. 'Promoted' also never means merged into this checkout -- promote_candidates lands into a disposable integration worktree/branch only; merging that into agent_env stays a human `git merge`.
_comment_test: The verify gate after a live write. Deliberately the WHOLE suite, not a scoped subset: write_allow permits tests/, so a candidate can write a test, and a scoped command would not necessarily run the file the candidate just added. -x stops at the first failure, which is the only outcome that matters to a gate. RE-EXAMINED 2026-07-29 against the argument that docs/ writes cannot break Python tests and so deserve a cheaper gate: that argument is FALSE here, measured. tests/test_comms.py:27 reads the real docs/COMMS_PROTOCOL.md, tests/test_generated_inventory.py reads the real docs/FEATURE_INVENTORY.json and docs/architecture-state.json, and tests/test_markdown_nodes.py:350 reads the real docs/HANDOFF.md. write_allow permits docs/, so a docs-only candidate can genuinely turn this suite red. The whole-suite command stays.
_comment_test_timeout: MEASURED 2026-07-29: this file declared the whole suite while verifier.verify() hard-coded timeout_s=120 and offload passed nothing else, so the committed configuration was STRUCTURALLY unable to pass -- every live write died with 'could not run tests: ... timed out after 120 seconds' and rolled back before the gate was ever reached. This budget is a RUNAWAY guard, not a performance target: it exists to stop a wedged pytest from pinning the harness, so it is sized well ABOVE the observed runtime rather than tightly around it. A false timeout is expensive in both directions -- good work is rolled back AND the task escalates to a paid lane -- and this box runs several agents at once, so a suite that takes ~20 min idle can take considerably longer under load. Hence roughly 2x headroom. Consequence to accept knowingly: every live write to docs/, tests/ or README.md now pays the full suite. The real fix for that is path-aware test selection (run only the tests reachable from what actually changed), which this static test_command cannot express; see the report accompanying this change.
